title: CAPIT FAQs | Data, Token, and Wallet Answers
description: Answers to common questions about CAPIT’s data, token mechanics, wallet flow, and claim boundaries.
headline: Frequently Asked Questions
body: Find clear, factual answers about CAPIT’s data ingestion, methodology, token flow, wallet interactions, and strict policy boundaries.

sections.heading: What is CAPIT?
sections.body: CAPIT is a public-facing environmental registry and utility token project built on the Base network. It organizes U.S. well-plugging records, explains their provenance, and mathematically links protocol activity next to the underlying data.

sections.heading: How does CAPIT verify that a well has been physically plugged?
sections.body: CAPIT relies entirely on public, state-level well registry data. A well is indexed only after the state agency officially confirms that downhole cement isolation and surface restoration are complete, assigning the well a formal status such as 'Plugged & Abandoned'.

sections.heading: What is the minting ratio for the CAPIT token?
sections.body: CAPIT operates under an absolute, non-inflationary 1:1 minting rule. Exactly one CAPIT token is minted for every unique, verified plugged-well record identified in official state filings.

sections.heading: Why is CAPIT built on the Base network?
sections.body: Base is a secure, low-cost Layer-2 blockchain network. It provides the high throughput and cryptographic security required to record high-volume environmental infrastructure records permanently on-chain.

sections.heading: Is CAPIT a carbon credit or emissions offset?
sections.body: No. CAPIT is strictly an environmental infrastructure receipt representing physical remediation work completed above and below ground. Tokens do not represent carbon credits, offsets, or speculative financial claims.

sections.heading: Do I need a crypto wallet to use the dashboard?
sections.body: No. The CAPIT National Well Plugging Dashboard is completely public and open to anyone. A self-custody wallet is only required if you choose to interact with protocol features.

sections.heading: How does CAPIT handle data corrections or state revisions?
sections.body: Public state registries are occasionally updated. CAPIT maintains an append-only, visible revision trail. If an agency modifies a record status, CAPIT logs the update transparently without altering the historical ledger.
